input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives us an express IBM defence and indemnity for third-party patent, trademark, copyright and trade-secret claims relating to Materials and Base Components IBM provides or uses in performing the Services, with the usual customer-side exclusions (Customer-provided items incorporated into Materials, Customer modifications, combinations with non-IBM products, and non-IBM hardware/software/data) — the fallback treats these exclusions as permitted, and the absence of an express "specifications" exclusion is favourable to us. The fallback remedies are all present: IBM must enable continued use, modify, or replace with functionally equivalent non-infringing items, and if none is reasonably available IBM credits the amounts we paid for the applicable Materials/Base Components (capped at twelve months of charges). On the super-cap element, Section 9.1(a) lists indemnification payments under Section 8.1 as a separate head of liability outside the $100,000/12-months monetary cap in 9.1(c), so IBM's IP indemnity is effectively uncapped — better than the 3× annual fees super-cap the fallback would accept. Notice, IBM control of the defence and our cooperation are the standard procedural conditions (with IBM reimbursing our above-nominal cooperation costs). This therefore sits at the fallback and is acceptable. Short of the preferred position, IBM's indemnity does not extend to breach of applicable law, IBM-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and our Section 8.2 indemnity is wider than Customer content plus breach of law (it also covers Customer Components IP claims, Services Recipient claims and mechanics' liens, mitigated by the 8.2(c) carve-back for IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach); we note these as gaps rather than redlining a bargain that meets the fallback.
